newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1-yr bond price seen up on good March CPI.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1-yr bond price seen up on good March CPI.

text.p: The minimum price of Poland's index-linked one-year bonds, to be auctioned on April 23, is likely to rise after the better-than-expected March inflation data, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.

"In view of the March inflation data, the yields of bonds, especially the one-year paper, are bound to fall -- not much perhaps, but fall," Piotr Dziewulski, head of the public debt department told Reuters.
At the last tender of the bonds on February 25, the minimum price was 94.48 and the average price was 94.62. The treasury will offer 200 million zlotys worth of the paper on April 23.
The Polish consumer price index rose 0.8 percent in March after a 1.1 percent rise in February, bringing the year-on-year index down to 16.6 percent from 17.3 percent in February.
The country's 26 biggest banks polled by Reuters in March had expected the month-on-month figure at 1.44 percent.
